label: Merge offset
type: the two-integer day-range pair defining the time window a scheduled or immediate backup:merge-task covers, where a lower integer represents a more recent day (0 = today). Documented under THREE different field-name spellings for what is otherwise the identical concept: `merge_offset_start`/`merge_offset_end` at plan level (backup-service.md), `offset_start`/`offset_end` on the immediate-trigger endpoint (backup-trigger-merge.md), and `merge_options.offset_start`/`merge_options.offset_end` nested under a `merge_options` object on couchbase-cli's own --task schema (couchbase-cli-backup-service-plan.md) - see docs-issues/server-backup-merge-offset-field-name-mismatch.
evidence: You set this time range by specifying two offsets, each representing a number of days. The `merge_offset_start` integer indicates the beginning of the range and the `merge_offset_end` integer the end.
The `merge-period-specification` must be a JSON document, containing the following: ... `offset_start` ... `offset_end`.
note: Kept as one concept covering all three spellings (per the extraction-layer id already in place from round 19) rather than split into separate ids, since no page disputes the semantics are identical - only the field name/nesting differs by surface. Round 29 (couchbase-cli-backup-service-plan.json) added the third spelling, confirming this is a CLI-vs-REST naming split as well as a plan-vs-trigger one. The naming inconsistency itself is logged as a docs-issue, not modeled as an ontology fact.
relates_to_competency_question: Is the merge day-range specified the same way at plan-schedule level as it is for an immediate/on-demand merge?
